item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"1br0 and 1ez3 should be interpreted only as partial observations of the syntaxin N-terminal Habc domain. SCOPe’s later treatment is to anchor the classification on the complete syntaxin N-terminal domain seen in 1dn1 chain B, and to subsume the earlier short constructs as fragments of that same domain rather than as independent evolutionary units defining a separate fold. Thus a fold assignment made from 1br0 or 1ez3 transfers only the local structural statement that their helices are syntaxin-N-terminal-domain fragments; it should not be used to infer that the excised fragments are complete autonomously folding domains, to choose them as full-domain representatives, or to propagate function/homology to unrelated proteins on the basis of a short helical match. Homology and functional annotation are safest at the syntaxin N-terminal family level, with 1dn1 chain B providing the full-domain template; fragment matches below that coverage are supporting evidence only when the missing Habc context is accounted for.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
